hypotheses.statement: ClayCode BASE receipts should separate content-addressed source/contract identity, canonical ProgramSemanticId, lowering identity, executable artifact identity and execution/replay identity instead of using one monolithic hash.
support: 5000 formatting/field-order cases produced 4958 source+contract identities but one canonical semantic identity and one generated artifact identity
semantic mutation changed semantic and artifact identity
parser-version-only mutation changed contract identity but not program semantics
lowerer-version mutation changed lowering/artifact identity but not program semantics
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One source/contract hash plus final execution receipt is sufficient and cheaper.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production Ubuntu matched tests show no stale-cache, replay, diagnosis or unsafe-reuse benefit from layered identities and material cost/repair harm.

hypotheses.statement: ProgramSemanticId should be derived at deterministic canonical typed IR (or an equivalently verified canonical semantic stage); pre-canonical Source/Parse stages may carry source/parse hashes and a non-authoritative expected semantic reference but must not independently mint semantic authority.
support: Lexical-closure run independently found ProgramSemanticId belongs post-parse/post-canonicalization
current Harness SourceChainEvidence v1 requires semantic_hash on source/parse/typed_ir, creating an ambiguous derivation-authority boundary
bounded formatting experiment shows many distinct source identities can map to one canonical semantic identity
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Copying the same semantic_hash across all chain stages is harmless and clearer provided artifact hashes are separate.
hypotheses.falsifier: A formal/production chain contract proves the source-stage semantic field is unambiguously non-authoritative, derivation-verifiable and cannot create circular or forged semantic evidence, with no replay/cache ambiguity.
